lesson_title: An Address for the Whole Planet
hook_text: Twenty-six degrees twelve minutes south, twenty-eight degrees three minutes east. That is not a code. It is Johannesburg's address.
clip_script: Wrap the Earth in imaginary belts and orange segments. The belts are latitude: how far north or south of the equator, up to ninety degrees at the poles. The segments are longitude: how far east or west of the line through Greenwich in London, up to one hundred and eighty. One degree is about a hundred and eleven kilometres, far too big to pin a town, so we chop each degree into sixty minutes, just like an hour. Now the address: latitude first, then longitude, always with the letters. Johannesburg: 26 degrees 12 minutes south, 28 degrees 3 minutes east. Forget the S and you have moved the city into the Northern Hemisphere. Swap the order and you have dropped it in the Northern Cape. Next time a cyclone hits Beira, look it up: 19 degrees 50 south, 34 degrees 51 east. Every headline has an address.
visual_style: A spinning whiteboard globe with belts and segments drawn on it, then a zoom to southern Africa with the coordinates of Johannesburg appearing letter by letter, and a pin dropping on Beira.
mood: Curious, precise, slightly dramatic about mistakes.
pacing: Steady build of the grid, a sharp beat on the two mistakes, a quick headline at the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find any place in the news in under a minute.
